examples.japanese: 彼が会議に遅刻した理由？それはね、電車が遅延したらしいんだ。まあ、私もそういう経験あるから、責められないけどね。
examples.english: The reason he was late for the meeting? Well, it seems the train was delayed. Well, I've had that experience too, so I can't really blame him.
examples.breakdown: Used to introduce an excuse or a reason that might be considered less than ideal, often with a nuance of 'because' or 'you see'.

examples.japanese: いくら説明しても、彼は理解しようとしないんだ。だって、そもそも聞く耳を持っていないんだから。
examples.english: No matter how much I explain, he doesn't try to understand. Because, fundamentally, he doesn't have an ear to listen.
examples.breakdown: Used to provide a strong, often slightly dismissive, reason for something, implying 'because' or 'since'.

examples.japanese: 新しいゲーム、面白そうだから買おうか迷ってるんだ。でも、お金が足りないんだよね。友達も買うって言ってたし、私も欲しいんだ。
examples.english: I'm hesitating about buying the new game because it looks interesting. But I don't have enough money. My friend said they're buying it too, and I want it.
examples.breakdown: Used to express a shared feeling or desire, similar to 'even' or 'too' in this context, referring to the friend's intention to buy.

N2.meaning: merely; nothing but; no more than

examples.japanese: 彼の提案は、単なる思いつきでしかない。実行可能性を検討すべきだ。
examples.english: His proposal is merely a whim. We should consider its feasibility.
examples.breakdown: The pattern でしかない is used after the noun 提案 (proposal) modified by 単なる (mere) to emphasize that it is nothing more than a whim.

examples.japanese: この仕事は、私にとっては経験を積むための手段でしかない。
examples.english: For me, this job is nothing more than a means to gain experience.
examples.breakdown: The pattern でしかない is used after the noun 手段 (means) to express that the job serves only the purpose of gaining experience.

examples.japanese: 彼が言うことは、いつも皮肉でしかないように聞こえる。
examples.english: Everything he says always sounds like mere sarcasm.
examples.breakdown: The pattern でしかない is used after the noun 皮肉 (sarcasm) to convey that his words are perceived as only sarcasm.

examples.japanese: 子供の頃の夢は、今となっては遠い過去の思い出でしかない。
examples.english: My childhood dreams are, now, merely distant memories of the past.
examples.breakdown: The pattern でしかない is used after the noun 思い出 (memory) to emphasize that the dreams are now just memories and nothing more.

examples.japanese: この問題の解決策は、一時しのぎでしかないだろう。
examples.english: The solution to this problem will likely be nothing more than a temporary fix.
examples.breakdown: The pattern でしかない is used after the noun 一時しのぎ (temporary fix) to indicate that the solution is only a temporary measure.

N2.meaning: not the time for; far from

examples.japanese: 仕事が山積みで、友達と遊びに行くどころではない。
examples.english: I have a mountain of work, so it's not the time to go out with friends.
examples.breakdown: The speaker is too busy with work (仕事が山積みで) to go out with friends (友達と遊びに行くどころではない).

examples.japanese: この状況では、冗談を言うどころではない。
examples.english: In this situation, it's far from the time to make jokes.
examples.breakdown: The current situation (この状況では) is too serious for joking (冗談を言うどころではない).

examples.japanese: 疲れていて、外食するどころか、家で簡単な食事をするので精一杯だった。
examples.english: I was so tired that I couldn't even think about eating out; I was barely able to make a simple meal at home.
examples.breakdown: The speaker was too tired (疲れていて) to go out to eat (外食するどころか), and even making a simple meal at home was difficult.

examples.japanese: 試験前なので、趣味のギターを弾くどころではない。
examples.english: Since it's before the exam, it's not the time to play my hobby guitar.
examples.breakdown: The speaker is focused on studying for the exam (試験前なので) and cannot afford to play guitar (趣味のギターを弾くどころではない).

examples.japanese: 緊急事態なので、個人的な用事を済ませるどころではない。
examples.english: This is an emergency, so it's not the time to take care of personal errands.
examples.breakdown: Due to the emergency (緊急事態なので), the speaker cannot deal with personal matters (個人的な用事を済ませるどころではない).

N2.meaning: far from; anything but; let alone

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事が忙しいどころか、毎日ゲームばかりしている。
examples.english: Far from being busy with work, he plays games every day.
examples.breakdown: どころか is used to contrast an expected or stated situation (being busy with work) with the actual, opposite reality (playing games).

examples.japanese: この料理は美味しいどころか、全く味がしない。
examples.english: Far from being delicious, this dish has no taste at all.
examples.breakdown: どころか highlights that the food is not just not delicious, but the opposite – it lacks any flavor.

examples.japanese: 試験に合格するどころか、今回は勉強もまともにできなかった。
examples.english: Far from passing the exam, I couldn't even study properly this time.
examples.breakdown: どころか emphasizes that the failure to pass the exam is an understatement, as the speaker couldn't even manage to study.

examples.japanese: 彼は将来有望などころか、最近はやる気もなさそうだ。
examples.english: Far from having a promising future, he seems to lack motivation lately.
examples.breakdown: どころか contrasts the positive expectation of a promising future with the current negative state of lacking motivation.

examples.japanese: この部屋は広いどころか、荷物を置くスペースもほとんどない。
examples.english: Far from being spacious, there's hardly any space to put luggage in this room.
examples.breakdown: どころか is used to show that the room is not only not spacious, but the opposite – it's very cramped.

N2.meaning: apparently; seems like; somehow

examples.japanese: どうやら明日は雨になりそうだ。
examples.english: Apparently, it looks like it's going to rain tomorrow.
examples.breakdown: どうやら is used to express a conclusion or guess based on some evidence or observation, suggesting that something seems to be the case.

examples.japanese: 彼は最近、仕事で何か大きな問題を抱えているようだが、どうやら口には出さない。
examples.english: He seems to have some big problem at work recently, but apparently he doesn't talk about it.
examples.breakdown: Here, どうやら indicates that the speaker is making a judgment or assumption about the situation, implying it's not directly confirmed but strongly suggested.

examples.japanese: この古い地図は、どうやら宝の隠し場所を示しているらしい。
examples.english: This old map apparently indicates the hiding place of a treasure.
examples.breakdown: どうやら is used to convey that the speaker has heard or believes something to be true, often with a sense of mystery or indirect information.

examples.japanese: 彼女の突然の退職は、どうやら個人的な理由によるものらしい。
examples.english: Her sudden resignation is apparently due to personal reasons.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses どうやら to express a likely reason for an event, based on speculation or unconfirmed information.

examples.japanese: いくら探しても見つからないと思ったら、どうやら鍵を家に忘れてきたようだ。
examples.english: When I thought I couldn't find it no matter how much I searched, it seems I left the keys at home.
examples.breakdown: どうやら is used here to express a realization or discovery after some effort, indicating a likely cause or situation.

N2.meaning: anyhow; in any case; at any rate

examples.japanese: 明日は雨が降るらしいから、どうせ家で過ごすことになるだろう。
examples.english: Tomorrow is supposed to rain, so I'll probably end up spending it at home anyway.
examples.breakdown: どうせ is used to express resignation or a sense of inevitability about a situation, often when the outcome is not ideal but cannot be avoided.

examples.japanese: この仕事は締め切りが近いし、難易度も高いから、どうせ徹夜する羽目になるだろう。
examples.english: The deadline for this work is near, and the difficulty is high, so I'll likely have to pull an all-nighter anyway.
examples.breakdown: どうせ is used here to anticipate a difficult or unpleasant outcome (pulling an all-nighter) due to existing circumstances (tight deadline, high difficulty).

examples.japanese: せっかくの休日なのに、天気が悪いなんて。どうせなら、ゆっくり寝ていよう。
examples.english: It's a precious holiday, but the weather is bad. Since that's the case, I might as well sleep in.
examples.breakdown: どうせ is used to express a resigned acceptance of a less-than-ideal situation and to choose a simple, passive course of action.

examples.japanese: 一生懸命勉強しても、試験に合格できるかどうか分からない。どうせなら、少しは楽しんだ方がいい。
examples.english: Even if I study hard, I don't know if I can pass the exam. If that's the case, I might as well have some fun.
examples.breakdown: どうせ is used to suggest that since the outcome is uncertain despite effort, it's better to prioritize enjoyment.

examples.japanese: あのレストランはいつも混んでいるから、予約なしで行ってもどうせ入れないだろう。
examples.english: That restaurant is always crowded, so even if I go without a reservation, I probably won't get in anyway.
examples.breakdown: どうせ is used to state a likely negative outcome based on past experience or common knowledge, implying that taking a certain action is futile.

N2.meaning: unable to; cannot; it is not possible to~

examples.japanese: 彼の突然の退職の理由は、私には知る由もない。
examples.english: There is no way for me to know the reason for his sudden resignation.
examples.breakdown: The verb 知る (shiru - to know) is used in its stem form (知り) and combined with 得ない (enai) to express inability to know.

examples.japanese: どんなに努力しても、経験不足ではこの仕事はこなせ得ないだろう。
examples.english: No matter how much I try, I probably won't be able to handle this job due to lack of experience.
examples.breakdown: The verb こなす (konasu - to handle/manage) is used in its stem form (こなせ) and combined with 得ない (enai) to express inability to handle something.

examples.japanese: この難解な数学の問題は、私のような素人には解読し得ない。
examples.english: This difficult math problem is impossible for an amateur like me to decipher.
examples.breakdown: The verb 解読する (kaidoku suru - to decipher/decode) is used in its stem form (解読し) and combined with 得ない (enai) to express inability to decipher.

examples.japanese: 長年の夢だったが、経済的な理由で独立する希望は叶え得なかった。
examples.english: It was my long-cherished dream, but for financial reasons, the hope of becoming independent could not be realized.
examples.breakdown: The verb 叶える (kanaeru - to fulfill/realize) is used in its stem form (叶え) and combined with 得ない (enai) to express inability to fulfill or realize something.

examples.japanese: 彼女の才能には驚かされるばかりで、追いつくことは望み得ない。
examples.english: I am constantly amazed by her talent, and I cannot hope to catch up.
examples.breakdown: The verb 望む (nozomu - to hope/wish) is used in its stem form (望み) and combined with 得ない (enai) to express inability to hope for something.

N2.meaning: can; to be able to; is possible to~

examples.japanese: 長年の努力が実を結び、ついに夢を叶えることができた。
examples.english: After many years of effort bore fruit, I was finally able to achieve my dream.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses the pattern verb-る + ことができ(る) + る to express the ability to achieve a dream through long-term effort.  It emphasizes the accomplishment.

examples.japanese: この新しいシステムを使えば、作業効率を大幅に向上させることができるでしょう。
examples.english: If you use this new system, you will likely be able to significantly improve work efficiency.
examples.breakdown: Here, verb-る + ことができる is used to talk about the potential or possibility of improving work efficiency with a new system. The 'でしょう' adds a nuance of likelihood.

examples.japanese: 限られた時間の中で、できる限りのことをやり遂げる必要がある。
examples.english: Within the limited time, it is necessary to accomplish as much as possible.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses the pattern verb-る + 限り + の + こと to express doing as much as one possibly can. It highlights the effort within constraints.

examples.japanese: 彼はどんな困難な状況でも、冷静さを失わずに対応する能力を得ている。
examples.english: He has acquired the ability to respond without losing his composure in any difficult situation.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses the pattern verb-る + 能力を得る to indicate the acquisition of a skill or ability, specifically the ability to remain calm in difficult situations.

examples.japanese: インターネットを使えば、世界中の情報に容易にアクセスすることが可能だ。
examples.english: If you use the internet, it is possible to easily access information from all over the world.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses the pattern verb-る + ことが可能だ, which is very similar to ことができる but often implies a more objective possibility or feasibility.

N2.meaning: again; once more

examples.japanese: 長い間会っていなかった友人と、昨日、駅で再び会うことができた。
examples.english: Yesterday, I was able to meet my friend, whom I hadn't seen for a long time, at the station again.
examples.breakdown: 再び is used here to indicate meeting the friend for a second time after a long interval.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトは一度中止になったが、多くの人の協力で再び動き出した。
examples.english: This project was canceled once, but it started moving again with the cooperation of many people.
examples.breakdown: 再び signifies that the project, which had stopped, has resumed its activity.

examples.japanese: 彼は一度失敗したが、諦めずに再び挑戦し、ついに成功した。
examples.english: He failed once, but without giving up, he challenged again and finally succeeded.
examples.breakdown: 再び emphasizes that he attempted the challenge for a second time after his initial failure.

examples.japanese: 長年使っていなかった古いカメラが、修理に出したら再び使えるようになった。
examples.english: The old camera, which I hadn't used for many years, became usable again after being sent for repair.
examples.breakdown: 再び indicates that the camera, after being out of use, is now functional once more.

examples.japanese: 雨で延期されていた試合が、今日、再び行われることになった。
examples.english: The game that was postponed due to rain will be held again today.
examples.breakdown: 再び is used to show that the game, which was supposed to happen earlier but was delayed, is now taking place.

N2.meaning: this way; that way; in such a way; how

examples.japanese: 先生の説明を聞いて、ようやく問題が解けるようになり、安心した。
examples.english: After listening to the teacher's explanation, I finally understood how to solve the problem, and felt relieved.
examples.breakdown: The pattern is used after a verb in the potential form (解ける) to indicate the manner or way in which something is done or becomes possible.

examples.japanese: 新しいプロジェクトの進め方について、皆の意見を参考にしながら、最善の方法を見つけ出すように努めます。
examples.english: Regarding how to proceed with the new project, I will strive to find the best method while taking everyone's opinions into consideration.
examples.breakdown: Here, '見つけ出すように' (to find in such a way) indicates the manner or goal of the effort.

examples.japanese: 彼女はいつも落ち着いた様子で、どんな困難な状況でも冷静に対処する。
examples.english: She always has a calm demeanor and deals with any difficult situation calmly.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses '様子で' (in such a way/manner) to describe her usual state or behavior.

examples.japanese: 子供たちが楽しく学べるように、先生は様々な工夫を凝らしている。
examples.english: The teacher is making various efforts so that the children can learn enjoyably.
examples.breakdown: '楽しく学べるように' (so that they can learn enjoyably) shows the purpose or the desired outcome of the teacher's actions.

examples.japanese: この料理は、素材の味を最大限に引き出すように調理するのがコツだ。
examples.english: The trick to this dish is to cook it in a way that maximizes the flavor of the ingredients.
examples.breakdown: '引き出すように' (in such a way that it draws out) describes the manner of cooking to achieve a specific result.

N2.meaning: as a result of; taking advantage of

examples.japanese: 友人の紹介がきっかけで、新しい趣味を見つけることができた。
examples.english: Thanks to my friend's introduction, I was able to find a new hobby.
examples.breakdown: 「友人の紹介」 (my friend's introduction) is the event that triggered the finding of a new hobby.

examples.japanese: テレビで見たドキュメンタリーがきっかけで、環境問題に関心を持つようになった。
examples.english: A documentary I saw on TV sparked my interest in environmental issues.
examples.breakdown: 「テレビで見たドキュメンタリー」 (the documentary I saw on TV) is the catalyst that led to the interest in environmental issues.

examples.japanese: 偶然見かけた求人広告がきっかけで、今の会社に転職することになった。
examples.english: A job advertisement I happened to see by chance led me to change jobs to my current company.
examples.breakdown: 「偶然見かけた求人広告」 (the job advertisement I happened to see by chance) served as the trigger for the job change.

examples.japanese: 先輩からのアドバイスがきっかけで、仕事の進め方が大きく改善された。
examples.english: My senior's advice became the turning point, and my way of proceeding with work greatly improved.
examples.breakdown: 「先輩からのアドバイス」 (my senior's advice) is the event that caused the significant improvement in work methods.

examples.japanese: 子供の頃に読んだSF小説がきっかけで、宇宙に強い興味を持つようになった。
examples.english: An SF novel I read as a child sparked a strong interest in space.
examples.breakdown: 「子供の頃に読んだSF小説」 (the SF novel I read as a child) is the event that initiated the strong interest in space.

N2.meaning: looks like; seems like; appears to

examples.japanese: 彼の顔色は悪く、何か病気でも患っているかのげだった。
examples.english: His complexion was bad, and he looked as if he were suffering from some illness.
examples.breakdown: Verb stem + げ: Describes an outward appearance or impression based on observation.

examples.japanese: 彼女は新しい仕事に張り切っているげで、毎日笑顔で出勤している。
examples.english: She seems to be enthusiastic about her new job, and she goes to work smiling every day.
examples.breakdown: Adjective (i-adj stem) + げ: Describes an outward appearance or impression based on observation.

examples.japanese: 古い洋館は、長い間人が住んでいないかのげな雰囲気を漂わせていた。
examples.english: The old Western-style house gave off an atmosphere as if no one had lived there for a long time.
examples.breakdown: Verb stem + げ: Describes an outward appearance or impression based on observation.

examples.japanese: 彼は難しい問題に直面しているげな表情をしていた。
examples.english: He had an expression that suggested he was facing a difficult problem.
examples.breakdown: Verb stem + げ: Describes an outward appearance or impression based on observation.

examples.japanese: 彼女の話し方には、何か隠しているげな響きがあった。
examples.english: There was something in the way she spoke that sounded as if she were hiding something.
examples.breakdown: Verb stem + げ: Describes an outward appearance or impression based on observation.

N2.meaning: conversely; on the contrary

examples.japanese: 彼はいつも楽観的だが、私の場合は逆に悲観的になりがちだ。
examples.english: He is always optimistic, but in my case, conversely, I tend to be pessimistic.
examples.breakdown: This sentence contrasts the speaker's tendency with another person's, using 逆に to indicate the opposite situation.

examples.japanese: この薬は眠気を催す効果があるが、人によっては逆に目が冴えてしまうこともあるらしい。
examples.english: This medicine has a drowsy effect, but it seems that for some people, conversely, it can make them more alert.
examples.breakdown: Here, 逆に is used to show an unexpected or opposite reaction that can occur in some individuals.

examples.japanese: もっと丁寧に話せば相手に好印象を与えるかと思いきや、逆に威圧感を与えてしまったようだ。
examples.english: I thought speaking more politely would give a good impression, but conversely, it seems I gave them an intimidating feeling.
examples.breakdown: This demonstrates a situation where an intended positive action had the opposite, negative effect, highlighted by 逆に.

examples.japanese: 忙しい時ほど休息が必要なのに、彼は逆に無理をして働き続けている。
examples.english: The busier you are, the more rest you need, but he, conversely, is overworking himself and continuing to push.
examples.breakdown: The sentence contrasts the expected action (rest when busy) with the actual action (overworking), using 逆に to emphasize the contradiction.

examples.japanese: その新しいシステムは効率を上げるはずだったが、逆に作業時間を増やす結果になった。
examples.english: That new system was supposed to increase efficiency, but conversely, it resulted in increasing work time.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses 逆に to point out that the outcome of a plan was the opposite of what was intended or expected.

N2.meaning: while, although; on the other hand

examples.japanese: この仕事は給料が高い反面、残業が多い。
examples.english: While this job pays well, on the other hand, it involves a lot of overtime.
examples.breakdown: This sentence contrasts two aspects of the same job: high salary (positive) and frequent overtime (negative).

examples.japanese: 彼はいつも明るいが、反面、時々落ち込んでいるように見える。
examples.english: He is always cheerful, but on the other hand, sometimes he seems depressed.
examples.breakdown: This sentence presents a contrast between his usual cheerful demeanor and occasional signs of sadness.

examples.japanese: 新しいパソコンは性能が良い反面、値段も高くなった。
examples.english: The new computer has good performance, but on the other hand, the price has also increased.
examples.breakdown: This sentence highlights a positive attribute (performance) and a negative consequence (high price) of the new computer.

examples.japanese: 都会は便利で刺激が多い反面、自然が少なく、騒がしいのが難点だ。
examples.english: While cities are convenient and full of excitement, on the other hand, they lack nature and are noisy, which is a drawback.
examples.breakdown: This sentence contrasts the advantages of city life (convenience, excitement) with its disadvantages (lack of nature, noise).

examples.japanese: 彼女は料理が上手な反面、掃除はあまり得意ではないようだ。
examples.english: While she is good at cooking, on the other hand, she doesn't seem very good at cleaning.
examples.breakdown: This sentence contrasts her skill in cooking with her lack of skill in cleaning.

N2.meaning: as was expected; sure enough; really

examples.japanese: 彼が本当に試験に合格できるか心配だったが、果たして彼は一番良い成績で合格した。
examples.english: I was worried if he could really pass the exam, but sure enough, he passed with the best score.
examples.breakdown: 果して (hatashite) is used here to confirm that something happened as expected or feared, often after a period of doubt or anticipation.

examples.japanese: 新しいレストランの評判はとても良かったが、果たして期待通り美味しい料理だった。
examples.english: The new restaurant's reputation was very good, and as expected, the food was delicious.
examples.breakdown: 果して (hatashite) confirms that the reality matched the high expectations or reputation.

examples.japanese: 長年探し求めていた情報が、果たしてこの古い文献の中にあった。
examples.english: The information I had been searching for for many years was, indeed, found within this old document.
examples.breakdown: 果して (hatashite) emphasizes that the sought-after information was actually discovered, fulfilling a long-held hope.

examples.japanese: あのチームが優勝候補だと言われていたが、果たしてその実力を証明した。
examples.english: That team was said to be the favorite to win, and they certainly proved their strength.
examples.breakdown: 果して (hatashite) confirms that the team lived up to its status as the favorite by demonstrating its true ability.

examples.japanese: 彼女の計画は無謀だと思ったが、果たして彼女はそれを成功させた。
examples.english: I thought her plan was reckless, but she really made it a success.
examples.breakdown: 果して (hatashite) expresses surprise and confirmation that the seemingly impossible plan was indeed achieved.

N2.meaning: more or less; pretty much; roughly

examples.japanese: 明日の会議の資料は一応準備しておきました。
examples.english: I've prepared the materials for tomorrow's meeting, more or less.
examples.breakdown: 一応 modifies the verb 準備しておきました (prepared), indicating that the preparation is done, but perhaps not perfectly or completely.

examples.japanese: このレシピ通りに作ったけど、味は一応美味しいと思う。
examples.english: I made it according to this recipe, and I think the taste is pretty much delicious.
examples.breakdown: 一応 modifies 美味しいと思う (think it's delicious), suggesting that while it might not be perfect, it's generally good.

examples.japanese: 体調は一応大丈夫ですが、少しだるいです。
examples.english: My physical condition is more or less okay, but I feel a bit sluggish.
examples.breakdown: 一応 modifies 大丈夫です (okay), implying that the condition isn't completely fine, but it's acceptable for now.

examples.japanese: 彼とは一応友達だけど、あまり親しくはない。
examples.english: He and I are friends, more or less, but we're not very close.
examples.breakdown: 一応 modifies 友達 (friends), indicating that the relationship can be categorized as friends, but with some reservation or lack of deep connection.

examples.japanese: この計画は一応成功したと言えるだろう。
examples.english: It's probably safe to say that this plan was more or less successful.
examples.breakdown: 一応 modifies 成功したと言えるだろう (can say it was successful), suggesting that the success might not be absolute or complete, but it achieved its basic goals.

N2.meaning: with the exception of; excepting

examples.japanese: このレストランでは、飲み物以外はすべて持ち込み可能です。
examples.english: In this restaurant, you can bring anything except for drinks.
examples.breakdown: Noun + 以外: 'except for drinks'

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事ができる人間以外、誰とも付き合わない。
examples.english: He doesn't associate with anyone except for people who are good at their jobs.
examples.breakdown: Noun + 以外: 'except for people who are good at their jobs'

examples.japanese: 週末は読書以外に特別な予定はありません。
examples.english: On weekends, I have no special plans other than reading.
examples.breakdown: Noun + 以外: 'other than reading'

examples.japanese: 彼女の意見以外は、すべて賛成です。
examples.english: I agree with everything except for her opinion.
examples.breakdown: Noun + 以外: 'except for her opinion'

examples.japanese: この地域では、車以外での移動は不便です。
examples.english: In this area, it is inconvenient to get around by means other than a car.
examples.breakdown: Noun + 以外: 'other than a car'

N2.meaning: more than; not less than; beyond

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトの成功は、私の予想以上に大きな達成感をもたらしました。
examples.english: The success of this project brought me a greater sense of accomplishment than I had expected.
examples.breakdown: 以上に is used after a noun (予想) to mean 'more than' or 'beyond' what was expected.

examples.japanese: 彼は単なる友人以上に、私の人生に大きな影響を与えた存在です。
examples.english: He is more than just a friend; he is someone who has had a great impact on my life.
examples.breakdown: 以上に is used after a noun (友人) to indicate something that goes beyond or is more than that category.

examples.japanese: 今回のキャンペーンは、目標売上高を大きく上回る結果となりました。
examples.english: This campaign resulted in sales figures that far exceeded our target.
examples.breakdown: 以上に is used after a noun phrase (目標売上高) to signify exceeding a certain level or amount.

examples.japanese: 彼女の芸術的才能は、単に優れているという以上に、見る者を感動させる力を持っています。
examples.english: Her artistic talent is more than just excellent; it has the power to move those who see it.
examples.breakdown: 以上に is used after a descriptive phrase (優れているという) to emphasize that the quality or impact goes beyond a simple description.

examples.japanese: 彼の献身的な働きぶりは、報酬以上に、チームからの信頼を得るためのものでした。
examples.english: His dedicated work ethic was not for reward, but for earning the trust of the team, and even more than that.
examples.breakdown: 以上に is used after a noun (報酬) to suggest that the motivation or outcome is greater than or goes beyond the stated reward.

N2.meaning: because; since; seeing that

examples.japanese: ここまで来てもらった以上は、必ず成功させなければならない。
examples.english: Since you've come this far, we absolutely must succeed.
examples.breakdown: 「以上は」 is used here to express a strong reason or obligation stemming from a preceding situation. Because you have come this far, there is a strong obligation to succeed.

examples.japanese: 彼が自分でそう言った以上は、もう何も言えない。
examples.english: Since he himself said so, I can't say anything more.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses 「以上は」 to indicate that a statement or action by someone else is the definitive reason for the speaker's current stance. Because he said it himself, there's no room for further comment.

examples.japanese: 大学を卒業した以上は、親に頼らず自立すべきだ。
examples.english: Now that you've graduated from university, you should be independent and not rely on your parents.
examples.breakdown: Here, 「以上は」 connects a completed action (graduating university) to an expected consequence or responsibility (becoming independent). Because graduation has happened, independence is expected.

examples.japanese: 約束した以上は、どんなことがあっても守るつもりです。
examples.english: Since I promised, I intend to keep it no matter what happens.
examples.breakdown: This demonstrates 「以上は」 as a basis for a strong commitment. Because a promise was made, the commitment to keep it is firm.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトに参加した以上は、最後まで責任を持ってやり遂げたい。
examples.english: Since I've participated in this project, I want to see it through to the end with responsibility.
examples.breakdown: 「以上は」 is used to establish the context of participation as the reason for the speaker's desire to fulfill their responsibilities until the end.

N2.meaning: abruptly; suddenly; all of a sudden

examples.japanese: 会議中に、彼は何も言わずにいきなり部屋を出て行った。
examples.english: During the meeting, he suddenly left the room without saying anything.
examples.breakdown: いきなり is used to describe an action that happened suddenly and unexpectedly, without any prior warning or preparation.

examples.japanese: 雨が降る気配もなかったのに、いきなり激しい雨になった。
examples.english: There was no sign of rain, but it suddenly became heavy rain.
examples.breakdown: いきなり emphasizes the abrupt change from no rain to heavy rain, highlighting the unexpectedness.

examples.japanese: 友人が私の家に来るというので、いきなり部屋を片付け始めた。
examples.english: My friend said they were coming over, so I suddenly started cleaning my room.
examples.breakdown: This sentence shows that the action of cleaning started abruptly upon hearing the news.

examples.japanese: 彼はいつも落ち着いている人なのに、いきなり大声で怒り出した。
examples.english: He's usually a calm person, but he suddenly started shouting angrily.
examples.breakdown: いきなり describes the sudden and out-of-character outburst of anger.

examples.japanese: 新しいプロジェクトの締め切りが、いきなり一週間早まった。
examples.english: The deadline for the new project was suddenly moved up by a week.
examples.breakdown: いきなり highlights the abrupt and unexpected change in the project deadline.

N2.meaning: in one go; without stopping; all at once

examples.japanese: 締め切りが近いので、レポートを完成させるために一気に書き上げた。
examples.english: Since the deadline is near, I wrote the report all at once to finish it.
examples.breakdown: 一気に is used here to describe completing the task of writing the report without stopping.

examples.japanese: 喉が渇いていたので、冷たい水をコップで一気に飲んだ。
examples.english: I was thirsty, so I drank the cold water from the glass in one go.
examples.breakdown: 一気に describes the action of drinking the water quickly and without pause.

examples.japanese: 彼はプロジェクトの難しい部分を一人で一気に片付けた。
examples.english: He tackled the difficult part of the project and finished it all by himself without stopping.
examples.breakdown: 一気に emphasizes that he handled and completed the challenging tasks in one continuous effort.

examples.japanese: 試験勉強が間に合わないと思い、週末はほぼ一気に勉強した。
examples.english: Thinking I wouldn't have enough time to study for the exam, I studied almost continuously over the weekend.
examples.breakdown: 一気に illustrates the intense and uninterrupted study session over the weekend.

examples.japanese: 新しい企画のアイデアが次々と浮かび、それを一気に資料にまとめた。
examples.english: New project ideas came to me one after another, and I compiled them into documents all at once.
examples.breakdown: 一気に describes the action of compiling the numerous ideas into documents without delay or interruption.

N2.meaning: on one hand, on the other hand

examples.japanese: この新しいプロジェクトはやりがいがある一方で、多くの困難も予想される。
examples.english: While this new project is rewarding, many difficulties are also anticipated.
examples.breakdown: 一方で is used to contrast two opposing ideas or situations within the same context.

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事熱心な一方で、家庭を顧みないところがある。
examples.english: On one hand, he is dedicated to his work, but on the other hand, he neglects his family.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses 一方で to present two contrasting aspects of a person's character or behavior.

examples.japanese: インターネットは情報収集に便利である一方で、誤った情報に惑わされる危険性もある。
examples.english: While the internet is convenient for gathering information, there is also a risk of being misled by incorrect information.
examples.breakdown: Here, 一方で highlights both the advantages and disadvantages of using the internet.

examples.japanese: 彼女は明るく社交的な一方で、内面には繊細な一面も持っている。
examples.english: On one hand, she is cheerful and sociable, but on the other hand, she also has a sensitive side to her inner self.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses 一方で to show a contrast between someone's outward appearance and their inner feelings or personality.

examples.japanese: この地域は自然が豊かである一方で、都市部へのアクセスが少し不便だ。
examples.english: While this region is rich in nature, access to urban areas is a bit inconvenient.
examples.breakdown: 一方で is used here to contrast a positive attribute (rich nature) with a negative one (inconvenient access).

N2.meaning: what is called; as it is called; so-called

examples.japanese: 彼は努力家で、いわゆる「天才肌」とは少し違うタイプだ。
examples.english: He is a hard worker, a different type from what is called a 'natural genius'.
examples.breakdown: いわゆる is used to introduce a commonly known or stereotypical term that the following noun phrase is being compared to or contrasted with.

examples.japanese: 最近、いわゆる「ミニマリスト」という生き方が注目されている。
examples.english: Recently, the lifestyle called 'minimalism' has been gaining attention.
examples.breakdown: いわゆる introduces a term or concept that is widely recognized or currently trending.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトは、いわゆる「失敗談」として語り継がれるだろう。
examples.english: This project will likely be passed down as what is called a 'failure story'.
examples.breakdown: いわゆる is used to label a situation or event with a common descriptive phrase.

examples.japanese: 彼女は、いわゆる「キャリアウーマン」として、仕事と家庭を両立させている。
examples.english: She is balancing work and family as a so-called 'career woman'.
examples.breakdown: いわゆる is used to categorize someone with a common societal label or stereotype.

examples.japanese: そのレストランは、いわゆる「隠れ家」的な雰囲気で、静かに食事ができる。
examples.english: That restaurant has a so-called 'hidden gem' atmosphere, allowing for a quiet meal.
examples.breakdown: いわゆる is used to describe a place or thing with a characteristic that is widely understood or sought after.

N2.meaning: at last; finally; beyond doubt

examples.japanese: 長い間待っていた旅行が、いよいよ明日から始まる。
examples.english: The trip I had been waiting for a long time finally begins tomorrow.
examples.breakdown: いよいよ is used to indicate that something long-awaited or anticipated is finally happening.

examples.japanese: 彼の努力が実を結び、いよいよプロのサッカー選手としてデビューする。
examples.english: His hard work has paid off, and he is finally debuting as a professional soccer player.
examples.breakdown: いよいよ emphasizes the culmination of effort and the imminent start of a new phase.

examples.japanese: 今年の夏は記録的な暑さになると予報されており、いよいよ本格的な夏がやってきたという感じだ。
examples.english: This summer is predicted to be record-breakingly hot, and it really feels like the real summer has finally arrived.
examples.breakdown: いよいよ conveys a sense of the situation reaching a significant point or a definitive stage.

examples.japanese: 会議の準備は全て整った。いよいよ本番だ。
examples.english: All preparations for the meeting are complete. It's finally showtime.
examples.breakdown: いよいよ signals the start of an important event after all preparations are done.

examples.japanese: 長引く不況から抜け出し、日本経済はいよいよ回復の兆しを見せ始めている。
examples.english: Emerging from the prolonged recession, the Japanese economy is finally beginning to show signs of recovery.
examples.breakdown: いよいよ expresses that a significant positive change is happening after a period of difficulty.

N2.meaning: for the sake of; from the standpoint of

examples.japanese: 子供たちの将来の上、両親はどんな困難にも耐えた。
examples.english: For the sake of their children's future, the parents endured any hardship.
examples.breakdown: 子供たちの将来の上 (kodomotachi no shōrai no ue) - for the sake of the children's future. The noun '将来' (future) is followed by 'の上'.

examples.japanese: 彼の立場の上では、その決定は当然だったと言えるだろう。
examples.english: From his standpoint, it can probably be said that the decision was natural.
examples.breakdown: 彼の立場の上では (kare no tachiba no ue de wa) - from his standpoint. The noun '立場' (standpoint/position) is followed by 'の上では'.

examples.japanese: 会社の存続の上、社員全員が協力しなければならない。
examples.english: For the sake of the company's survival, all employees must cooperate.
examples.breakdown: 会社の存続の上 (kaisha no sonzoku no ue) - for the sake of the company's survival. The noun '存続' (survival) is followed by 'の上'.

examples.japanese: 国民の安全の上、政府はあらゆる対策を講じている。
examples.english: For the sake of the citizens' safety, the government is taking all possible measures.
examples.breakdown: 国民の安全の上 (kokumin no anzen no ue) - for the sake of the citizens' safety. The noun '安全' (safety) is followed by 'の上'.

examples.japanese: 趣味の上では、時間もお金も惜しまない人がいる。
examples.english: When it comes to hobbies, there are people who spare neither time nor money.
examples.breakdown: 趣味の上では (shumi no ue de wa) - when it comes to hobbies/from the standpoint of hobbies. The noun '趣味' (hobby) is followed by 'の上では'.

N2.meaning: as if; just like

examples.japanese: 彼は何も知らないかのように、平然と振る舞っていた。
examples.english: He behaved as if he knew nothing.
examples.breakdown: Used after a verb in the plain form to describe an action or state that is contrary to the actual situation, implying a pretense.

examples.japanese: 彼女はまるで長年の友人であるかのように、私に話しかけてきた。
examples.english: She spoke to me as if we were long-time friends.
examples.breakdown: Connects a noun or pronoun (with まるで for emphasis) to an action or state, suggesting a comparison to something unreal or imagined.

examples.japanese: その新しいソフトウェアは、まるで魔法がかかったかのように、難しい作業を簡単にこなした。
examples.english: The new software handled difficult tasks easily, as if by magic.
examples.breakdown: Used with a noun phrase to describe a situation or action that seems extraordinary or unbelievable.

examples.japanese: 子供たちは、宝物を見つけたかのように、興奮して走り回っていた。
examples.english: The children were running around excitedly as if they had found treasure.
examples.breakdown: Follows a verb in the past plain form to describe an action that resembles a past event or state.

examples.japanese: 彼は試験に落ちたのに、合格したかのように嬉しそうにしていた。
examples.english: Even though he failed the exam, he looked happy as if he had passed.
examples.breakdown: Used with a verb in the past plain form to express a situation that is contrary to the truth, highlighting a deceptive or false appearance.

N2.meaning: just when; no sooner than

examples.japanese: さっきまで雨が降っていたかと思ったら、もう晴れてきた。
examples.english: Just when I thought it was raining until a moment ago, it's already cleared up.
examples.breakdown: Used to express a sudden change or unexpected turn of events, contrasting the previous state with the current one.

examples.japanese: 彼はいつも真面目な人だと思っていたら、実は冗談ばかり言う人だった。
examples.english: I thought he was always a serious person, but it turned out he's actually someone who tells jokes all the time.
examples.breakdown: Indicates that a prior assumption or belief about someone or something was proven wrong by a subsequent realization.

examples.japanese: 会議が終わったかと思ったら、次の議題に移っていた。
examples.english: No sooner than the meeting ended, we had already moved on to the next agenda item.
examples.breakdown: Highlights the quick succession of events, where one action or state is immediately followed by another.

examples.japanese: この仕事は簡単だと思っていたら、予想以上に複雑で時間がかかった。
examples.english: Just when I thought this job was easy, it turned out to be more complicated than I expected and took a lot of time.
examples.breakdown: Expresses a contrast between an initial expectation (easy) and the reality (complicated and time-consuming).

examples.japanese: ようやく落ち着いたかと思ったら、また新しい問題が起こった。
examples.english: Just when I thought things had finally settled down, another new problem arose.
examples.breakdown: Emphasizes the feeling of relief being short-lived due to the immediate occurrence of a new issue.

examples.japanese: 彼は周囲の反対を敢えて押し切り、自分の信念を貫いた。
examples.english: He deliberately ignored the surrounding opposition and followed his own beliefs.
examples.breakdown: 敢えて is used here to emphasize that he intentionally went against others' opinions.

examples.japanese: 忙しい時こそ、気分転換に敢えて遠出をすることがある。
examples.english: Precisely when I'm busy, I sometimes deliberately take a long trip to refresh my mood.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses 敢えて to highlight the intentional act of taking a trip despite being busy.

examples.japanese: その問題の複雑さを考えると、敢えて単純な解決策を提案するのは勇気がいる。
examples.english: Considering the complexity of that problem, it takes courage to deliberately propose a simple solution.
examples.breakdown: Here, 敢えて suggests a conscious choice to offer a seemingly inadequate solution, implying a deeper strategy or a test.

examples.japanese: ベテランの料理人は、あえて伝統的な調理法にこだわり、素材本来の味を引き出す。
examples.english: The veteran chef deliberately sticks to traditional cooking methods to bring out the inherent flavor of the ingredients.
examples.breakdown: 敢えて emphasizes the chef's intentional adherence to tradition, even when other methods might be easier.

examples.japanese: 失敗を恐れず、敢えて新しい分野に挑戦することが、自己成長に繋がるだろう。
examples.english: Daring to challenge new fields without fear of failure will likely lead to personal growth.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses 敢えて to express the idea of intentionally taking on a challenge, even if it involves risk.

N1.meaning: to the end; persistently; is still very ~

examples.japanese: 彼はあくまでも自分の意見を譲らず、議論は平行線をたどった。
examples.english: He stubbornly refused to yield his opinion, and the discussion remained at a standstill.
examples.breakdown: あくまでも is used here to emphasize that he persistently held onto his opinion, refusing to change it.

examples.japanese: これはあくまでも個人的な意見であり、会社の公式見解ではありません。
examples.english: This is strictly a personal opinion and not the official stance of the company.
examples.breakdown: あくまでも emphasizes that the opinion is solely personal and not meant to represent anything beyond that.

examples.japanese: たとえ困難に直面しても、あくまでも目標達成のために努力を続けるつもりだ。
examples.english: Even if I face difficulties, I intend to persistently strive to achieve my goal.
examples.breakdown: あくまでも highlights the unwavering determination to continue working towards the goal, no matter the obstacles.

examples.japanese: その伝統工芸品は、現代的なデザインを取り入れつつも、あくまでも昔ながらの製法を守っている。
examples.english: While incorporating modern designs, that traditional craft still strictly adheres to the old methods of production.
examples.breakdown: あくまでも emphasizes that despite modern adaptations, the core, traditional methods are still being maintained to the end.

examples.japanese: 彼女はどんなに反対されても、あくまでも自分の夢を追い続ける覚悟を決めていた。
examples.english: No matter how much she was opposed, she was determined to persistently pursue her dream.
examples.breakdown: あくまでも underscores her resolute commitment to continue chasing her dream without giving up.

N1.meaning: just as one thought; sure enough

examples.japanese: 彼はいつもギリギリにしか来ないと思っていたが、案の定、今日の会議にも遅刻してきた。
examples.english: I thought he would always come at the last minute, and sure enough, he was late for today's meeting too.
examples.breakdown: 案の定 is used to indicate that something happened exactly as expected or feared.

examples.japanese: 長年の経験から、このプロジェクトは失敗すると予感していた。案の定、いくつかの問題が発生し、計画通りに進まなかった。
examples.english: From years of experience, I had a premonition that this project would fail. Just as I thought, several problems occurred, and it didn't proceed as planned.
examples.breakdown: This sentence shows 案の定 confirming a negative prediction based on experience.

examples.japanese: 友人が新しいビジネスを始めたが、あまりにも楽観的すぎると感じていた。案の定、数ヶ月後には経営難に陥ったらしい。
examples.english: My friend started a new business, but I felt he was too optimistic. Sure enough, it seems he ran into financial difficulties a few months later.
examples.breakdown: Here, 案の定 is used to confirm a suspicion about a friend's venture.

examples.japanese: この地域の天気予報はあまり当てにならない。案の定、晴れると予報されていたのに、激しい雨が降ってきた。
examples.english: The weather forecast for this region is not very reliable. Just as I thought, even though it was predicted to be sunny, heavy rain started falling.
examples.breakdown: This example demonstrates 案の定 in relation to the unreliability of a forecast.

examples.japanese: あの作家の新作は、期待していたほどの内容ではなかった。案の定、多くの批評家から厳しい評価を受けていた。
examples.english: The new work by that author was not as good as I had expected. Sure enough, it received harsh reviews from many critics.
examples.breakdown: 案の定 confirms a negative expectation about a literary work's reception.

examples.japanese: 旅行の計画は、出発の前にあらかじめ立てておくのが良いだろう。
examples.english: It's probably best to make travel plans beforehand, before departure.
examples.breakdown: あらかじめ is used here to indicate that the action of making travel plans should be done in advance of the trip.

examples.japanese: 会議で質問されそうなことは、あらかじめ調べて資料を準備しておきました。
examples.english: I looked into things that might be asked during the meeting and prepared materials in advance.
examples.breakdown: あらかじめ modifies the verb 調べる (to investigate/look into), emphasizing that this preparation was done beforehand.

examples.japanese: この地域の天気は変わりやすいので、外出する際はあらかじめ天気予報を確認することをお勧めします。
examples.english: The weather in this region changes easily, so we recommend checking the weather forecast beforehand when you go out.
examples.breakdown: あらかじめ is used to stress the importance of checking the weather forecast in advance of going out.

examples.japanese: 新しいプロジェクトの成功のためには、リスク要因をあらかじめ洗い出し、対策を講じる必要がある。
examples.english: To ensure the success of the new project, it is necessary to identify risk factors beforehand and take countermeasures.
examples.breakdown: あらかじめ modifies 洗い出す (to identify/wash out), indicating that the identification of risk factors should happen in advance.

examples.japanese: このレストランは人気があるので、週末に食事をするなら、あらかじめ予約を入れておくことを強く推奨します。
examples.english: This restaurant is popular, so if you plan to dine on the weekend, we strongly recommend making a reservation in advance.
examples.breakdown: あらかじめ is used to emphasize that reservations should be made beforehand due to the restaurant's popularity.

N1.meaning: which can exist solely due to

examples.japanese: この素晴らしい成果は、チームメンバー全員の協力があってのものです。
examples.english: This wonderful achievement is solely due to the cooperation of all team members.
examples.breakdown: The pattern 'あっての' is used to indicate that the '素晴らしい成果' (wonderful achievement) can only exist because of 'チームメンバー全員の協力' (the cooperation of all team members).

examples.japanese: 長年の経験があっての、このベテラン職人の技は他では見られない。
examples.english: This veteran craftsman's skill, which can only exist due to many years of experience, cannot be seen elsewhere.
examples.breakdown: '長年の経験' (many years of experience) is the essential condition for the existence of 'このベテラン職人の技' (this veteran craftsman's skill), as indicated by 'あっての'.

examples.japanese: 家族の理解と支えがあっての、私の今日の成功がある。
examples.english: My success today exists solely due to the understanding and support of my family.
examples.breakdown: The pattern 'あっての' emphasizes that '私の今日の成功' (my success today) is entirely dependent on '家族の理解と支え' (the understanding and support of my family).

examples.japanese: 地域住民の協力があっての、この祭りは毎年成功している。
examples.english: This festival is successful every year solely due to the cooperation of the local residents.
examples.breakdown: '地域住民の協力' (the cooperation of the local residents) is presented as the indispensable factor for the continued success of 'この祭り' (this festival), using 'あっての'.

examples.japanese: 健康な体があっての、人生のあらゆる楽しみを享受できるのだ。
examples.english: One can enjoy all of life's pleasures solely due to a healthy body.
examples.breakdown: The phrase '健康な体' (a healthy body) is highlighted as the fundamental prerequisite for '人生のあらゆる楽しみ' (all of life's pleasures) to exist, demonstrated by 'あっての'.

examples.japanese: 子供の将来のためを思えばこそ、厳しく指導するのです。
examples.english: It is precisely because I think of my child's future that I guide them strictly.
examples.breakdown: The verb 思えば is in the conditional form, followed by こそ to emphasize 'precisely because'.

examples.japanese: 彼の実力を信じているがゆえにこそ、この重要な仕事を任せたい。
examples.english: It is precisely because I believe in his abilities that I want to entrust him with this important job.
examples.breakdown: The noun 実力 is followed by がゆえに (a more formal way of saying 'because'), which is then followed by こそ for emphasis.

examples.japanese: どんなに苦しくても、諦めないでいればこそ、今日の成功がある。
examples.english: It is precisely because I didn't give up, no matter how difficult it was, that I have today's success.
examples.breakdown: The verb 諦めないでいる is in the negative conditional form, followed by いればこそ to emphasize the reason for success.

examples.japanese: 多くの人に支持されているからこそ、この政策は実行されるべきだ。
examples.english: It is precisely because it is supported by many people that this policy should be implemented.
examples.breakdown: The verb 支持されている is in the passive conditional form, followed by からこそ to emphasize the reason for the policy's implementation.

examples.japanese: 長年の努力があってこそ、このような素晴らしい作品が完成する。
examples.english: It is precisely because of years of effort that such a wonderful work can be completed.
examples.breakdown: The noun phrase 長年の努力があって is in the conditional form, followed by こそ to emphasize the essential role of the effort.

N1.pattern: ばそれまでだ /たらそれまでだ
N1.romanization: ba sore made da / tara sore made da

examples.japanese: 努力を怠れば、せっかく築き上げたキャリアもそれまでだ。
examples.english: If you neglect your efforts, even the career you've worked hard to build will be over.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses the pattern '～ばそれまでだ' to express that neglecting efforts will lead to the end of one's career, implying a severe consequence.

examples.japanese: この病気は早期発見ができないと、手遅れになったらそれまでだと言われている。
examples.english: It is said that if this disease cannot be detected early, then it's over once it becomes too late to treat.
examples.breakdown: Here, '～たらそれまでだ' highlights the critical importance of early detection in a medical context, suggesting that without it, the situation becomes irreversible.

examples.japanese: いくら才能があっても、練習しなければ、プロの世界ではそれまでだ。
examples.english: No matter how talented you are, if you don't practice, it's over in the professional world.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses '～ばそれまでだ' to emphasize that talent alone is insufficient for success in a professional field; consistent practice is essential, or one's potential will go to waste.

examples.japanese: せっかくの旅行なのに、天気が悪かったら台無しになってそれまでだ。
examples.english: It's a precious trip, but if the weather is bad, it will be ruined and that's that.
examples.breakdown: The pattern '～たらそれまでだ' is used to express disappointment, indicating that bad weather would completely spoil the enjoyment of a highly anticipated trip.

examples.japanese: 借金を返済できなくなれば、会社は倒産してそれまでだ。
examples.english: If we can no longer repay our debts, the company will go bankrupt and that will be the end of it.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses '～ばそれまでだ' to describe a dire business situation where the inability to repay debts leads to bankruptcy, signifying the complete downfall of the company.

N1.pattern: べからず / べからざる
N1.meaning: must not; should not; do not ~

examples.japanese: この資料は機密情報につき、許可なく外部に持ち出すべからず。
examples.english: As this document contains confidential information, you must not take it outside without permission.
examples.breakdown: 「持ち出すべからず」 is used to state a strict prohibition in a formal context, often seen in notices or regulations.

examples.japanese: 長年の努力も虚しく、彼の夢は叶うべからざるものとなった。
examples.english: Despite years of effort, his dream became something that could not be realized.
examples.breakdown: 「叶うべからざるもの」 uses the attributive form 「べからざる」 to modify the noun 「もの」, indicating something that should not or cannot happen.

examples.japanese: 試験会場では、携帯電話の使用を厳禁とする。違反者は退場処分とするべからず。
examples.english: Use of mobile phones is strictly prohibited in the examination hall. Violators must not be expelled.
examples.breakdown: 「処分とするべからず」 is a strong imperative to not perform a certain action, typically in rules or warnings.

examples.japanese: 未来の世代に美しい自然を残すことは、我々が果たすべき、譲ることべからざる責務である。
examples.english: Leaving beautiful nature for future generations is a responsibility we must fulfill, one that cannot be conceded.
examples.breakdown: 「譲ることべからざる責務」 uses 「べからざる」 to describe a noun (責務) that must not be given up or compromised.

examples.japanese: 公共の場での喫煙は、周囲の人々への配慮として、控えるべきである。ここでは禁煙と明記されているので、吸うべからず。
examples.english: Smoking in public places should be refrained from out of consideration for others. Since it is clearly stated here that smoking is prohibited, you must not smoke.
examples.breakdown: 「吸うべからず」 is a direct and strong prohibition, often used in signs or explicit instructions to not do something.

N1.meaning: in order to; for the purpose of ~

examples.japanese: 成功を収めるべく、彼は連日深夜まで研究に没頭した。
examples.english: In order to achieve success, he immersed himself in research late into the night every day.
examples.breakdown: Verb stem (masu-form without -masu) + べく. Used to express the purpose of an action, often in more formal or serious contexts.

examples.japanese: 地球環境を守るべく、私たちは省エネ活動を推進しなければならない。
examples.english: In order to protect the global environment, we must promote energy-saving activities.
examples.breakdown: Verb stem + べく. Indicates the strong purpose or intention behind an action, emphasizing the importance of the goal.

examples.japanese: 将来のキャリアアップを図るべく、語学学校に通い始めた。
examples.english: In order to aim for future career advancement, I started attending a language school.
examples.breakdown: Verb stem + べく. Expresses the purpose of a personal endeavor, often related to self-improvement or future goals.

examples.japanese: 会議で発言する機会を得るべく、彼は事前に資料を徹底的に読み込んだ。
examples.english: In order to gain an opportunity to speak at the meeting, he thoroughly read through the materials beforehand.
examples.breakdown: Verb stem + べく. Shows the preparatory action taken for a specific future event or outcome.

examples.japanese: 人々の健康増進に貢献すべく、最新の医療技術の研究に励んでいる。
examples.english: In order to contribute to the improvement of people's health, I am diligently researching the latest medical technologies.
examples.breakdown: Verb stem + べく. Used to state a noble or altruistic purpose driving one's actions.

examples.japanese: 長年の努力もむなしく、彼はついに目標を達成することはできず、落胆を隠すべくもなかった。
examples.english: Despite years of effort, he ultimately could not achieve his goal, and he couldn't hide his disappointment.
examples.breakdown: The verb 隠す (kakusu - to hide) is in its dictionary form, followed by べくもない, indicating that it was impossible to hide his disappointment.

examples.japanese: 突然の解雇通知に、彼女はただただ呆然とするべくもなく、言葉を失った。
examples.english: Upon receiving the sudden dismissal notice, she was simply stunned and lost for words, unable to do anything but stare blankly.
examples.breakdown: The verb 呆然とする (bōzen to suru - to be stunned/dumbfounded) is in its dictionary form, followed by べくもない, signifying that she could not possibly react in any other way.

examples.japanese: 専門家でさえ、この複雑な問題を解決する確実な方法を見出すことはできず、皆途方に暮れるばかりだった。
examples.english: Even the experts couldn't find a sure way to solve this complex problem, and everyone was simply at a loss.
examples.breakdown: The verb 見出す (miidasu - to find/discover) is in its dictionary form, followed by べくもない, conveying that it was impossible for even experts to find a solution.

examples.japanese: 長年研究してきたテーマが時代遅れになってしまい、彼の努力は報われるべくもなかった。
examples.english: The theme he had researched for many years became outdated, and his efforts could not be rewarded.
examples.breakdown: The verb 報われる (mukuwareru - to be rewarded) is in its dictionary form, followed by べくもない, meaning his efforts were unable to be rewarded.

examples.japanese: あまりにも大きな災害であったため、復旧の見通しは立たず、人々は希望を持つべくもなかった。
examples.english: Because it was such a massive disaster, there was no prospect of recovery, and people could not possibly hold onto hope.
examples.breakdown: The verb 持つ (motsu - to hold) is in its dictionary form, followed by べくもない, indicating that it was impossible for people to maintain hope.

examples.japanese: 長年の努力が実を結び、彼はついに社長になるべくしてなった。
examples.english: After many years of hard work bore fruit, he naturally became the president.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses べくして after the verb 実を結び (to bear fruit), indicating that becoming president was an inevitable outcome of his long-term efforts.

examples.japanese: その才能あふれる若手俳優は、スターになるべくして生まれてきたかのようだ。
examples.english: That talented young actor seems to have been born to become a star.
examples.breakdown: べくして is used with 生まれてきた (was born) to express that his birth and talent were destined for stardom.

examples.japanese: 環境破壊が進みすぎた結果、異常気象が頻発するべくしてしている。
examples.english: As a result of excessive environmental destruction, abnormal weather is occurring as it is bound to.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses べくして with している (is occurring) to show that the frequent occurrence of abnormal weather is an unavoidable consequence of environmental destruction.

examples.japanese: 彼の専門知識と経験を考慮すれば、そのプロジェクトのリーダーに選ばれるべくして選ばれたと言える。
examples.english: Considering his expertise and experience, it can be said that he was naturally chosen as the leader for that project.
examples.breakdown: べくして is used with 選ばれた (was chosen) to imply that his selection was a logical and expected outcome of his qualifications.

examples.japanese: 長年チームを支えてきたベテラン選手は、引退するべくして引退した。
examples.english: The veteran player who supported the team for many years retired as was bound to happen.
examples.breakdown: べくして is used with 引退した (retired) to suggest that his retirement was a natural and expected progression after his long career.

N1.pattern: びる / びて / びた
N1.meaning: to seem to be; to appear; to behave as ~

examples.japanese: 彼は最近、何か隠しているかのように、落ち着かない様子でいる。
examples.english: He seems to be hiding something lately, as he's acting restless.
examples.breakdown: 落ち着かない様子でいる (ositsukanai yousu de iru) + びる -> 落ち着かない様子でびる (ositsukanai yousu de biru) - to seem to be in a restless state.

examples.japanese: 長年の努力が実を結び、ついに彼は成功者びて見えるようになった。
examples.english: His years of effort have paid off, and he finally appears to be a successful person.
examples.breakdown: 成功者 (seikousha) + びる -> 成功者びる (seikousha biru) - to seem to be a successful person.

examples.japanese: 彼女はいつも朗らかで、周りの人を明るくするような雰囲気を持っていた。
examples.english: She was always cheerful and had an atmosphere that made those around her seem bright.
examples.breakdown: 明るくするような雰囲気 (akaruku suru you na fun'iki) + を持っていた (wo motte ita) -> 明るくするような雰囲気を持びていた (akaruku suru you na fun'iki wo mottte ita) - to seem to possess an atmosphere that brightens others.

examples.japanese: その老舗の店は、歴史を感じさせるような重厚な雰囲気を漂わせていた。
examples.english: That long-established shop exuded a dignified atmosphere, making it seem as if it held history.
examples.breakdown: 歴史を感じさせるような (rekishi wo kanjisaseru you na) + 重厚な雰囲気 (juukou na fun'iki) + を漂わせていた (wo tadayowasete ita) -> 歴史を感じさせるような重厚な雰囲気を漂わせびていた (rekishi wo kanjisaseru you na juukou na fun'iki wo tadayowasebite ita) - to seem to be exuding a dignified atmosphere that makes one feel history.

examples.japanese: 彼は長年研究に没頭していたせいか、どこか浮世離れしたような雰囲気を持っていた。
examples.english: Perhaps because he had been engrossed in research for many years, he had an atmosphere that seemed somewhat detached from the mundane world.
examples.breakdown: 浮世離れしたような (ukiyo banare shita you na) + 雰囲気を持っていた (fun'iki wo motte ita) -> 浮世離れしたような雰囲気を持びていた (ukiyo banare shita you na fun'iki wo mottte ita) - to seem to possess an atmosphere that is detached from the mundane world.

examples.japanese: 彼の仕事のやりっぷりは、ベテランの域に達していると言えるだろう。
examples.english: His way of working can be said to have reached the level of a veteran.
examples.breakdown: 仕事のやりっぷり (shigoto no yaripuri) means 'the way of doing work'. っぷり is used here to describe the manner or style of his work.

examples.japanese: 長年離れていた故郷の変わりっぷりに、彼は目を丸くした。
examples.english: He widened his eyes at the way his hometown had changed after being away for many years.
examples.breakdown: 変わりっぷり (kawarippuri) means 'the way of changing' or 'how much it has changed'. っぷり emphasizes the extent or manner of the change.

examples.japanese: 彼女の話しぶりからは、自信と経験が滲み出ている。
examples.english: From her manner of speaking, confidence and experience emanate.
examples.breakdown: 話しぶり (hanashiburi) means 'manner of speaking' or 'way of talking'. ぶり is used to describe the style or characteristic of her speech.

examples.japanese: あの画家は、独特の筆遣いのぶりで知られている。
examples.english: That painter is known for his unique way of brushwork.
examples.breakdown: 筆遣いのぶり (fudetukai no buri) means 'manner of brushwork' or 'style of using the brush'. ぶり describes the specific technique or style.

examples.japanese: 子供たちの無邪気な笑いっぷりを見ていると、心が和む。
examples.english: Watching the innocent way the children laugh makes my heart feel at ease.
examples.breakdown: 笑いっぷり (waraipuri) means 'the way of laughing' or 'how they laugh'. っぷり here describes the lively and innocent manner of their laughter.

N1.pattern: ぶる / ぶって / ぶった
N1.meaning: behaving like; to pretend / act like ~

examples.japanese: 長年の努力もむなしく、彼は成功の喜びを味わうことさえできなかった。
examples.english: Despite his years of effort, he couldn't even savor the joy of success.
examples.breakdown: The pattern 「〜ことさえできなかった」 (couldn't even ~) uses 「さえ」 which is synonymous with 「だに」 in this context, emphasizing the inability to achieve something even with effort.

examples.japanese: 彼女はあまりにも疲れていたので、ベッドに倒れ込むやいなや、眠りに落ちた。夢を見るだにしないほどだった。
examples.english: She was so tired that as soon as she fell onto the bed, she fell asleep. She was so tired she didn't even dream.
examples.breakdown: 「夢を見るだにしない」 means 'not even to dream', emphasizing the extreme exhaustion.

examples.japanese: 彼は複雑な問題を前にしても、顔色一つ変えなかった。驚きを示すだにしない冷静さだった。
examples.english: Even when faced with a complex problem, he didn't change his expression. His composure was such that he didn't even show surprise.
examples.breakdown: 「驚きを示すだにしない」 means 'not even to show surprise', highlighting his unruffled demeanor.

examples.japanese: そのニュースを聞いた時、信じられない気持ちになったが、それを口にするだにためらった。
examples.english: When I heard that news, I felt disbelief, but I hesitated even to voice it.
examples.breakdown: 「口にするだにためらった」 means 'hesitated even to say it', indicating a strong reluctance to express disbelief.

examples.japanese: 子供たちは新しいおもちゃに夢中になり、他のことに気を取られるだにしない様子だった。
examples.english: The children were engrossed in their new toys, showing no signs of being distracted by anything else.
examples.breakdown: 「気を取られるだにしない」 means 'not even to be distracted', emphasizing their complete focus on the toys.

N1.meaning: and; and the like; and so forth ~

examples.japanese: 彼は会議で遅刻するだの、資料を忘れるだのと、言い訳ばかりしていた。
examples.english: In the meeting, he kept making excuses, such as being late and forgetting documents.
examples.breakdown: だの〜だの is used to list multiple negative or annoying examples, implying a general sense of complaint or dissatisfaction.

examples.japanese: 週末は、読書するだの、映画を見るだのと、家でゆっくり過ごしたい。
examples.english: On the weekend, I want to spend time relaxing at home, doing things like reading books and watching movies.
examples.breakdown: Here, だの〜だの lists enjoyable, relaxing activities, conveying a desire for a peaceful weekend.

examples.japanese: 彼女は、ブランド品を買うだの、高級レストランに行くといった、贅沢な生活を続けている。
examples.english: She continues to live a luxurious life, buying designer goods and going to high-end restaurants.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses だの〜だの to exemplify the extravagant nature of her lifestyle.

examples.japanese: 子供たちは、公園で走り回るだの、滑り台で遊ぶだのと、元気いっぱいだった。
examples.english: The children were full of energy, running around in the park and playing on the slide.
examples.breakdown: だの〜だの is used to list energetic and playful activities that children engage in.

examples.japanese: 仕事が終わらないだの、給料が安いだのと、不満ばかり言っていても何も変わらない。
examples.english: Just complaining about things like not finishing work or having low pay won't change anything.
examples.breakdown: This sentence employs だの〜だの to list common complaints, emphasizing the futility of such expressions without action.

examples.japanese: 彼は一生懸命勉強しただろうに、試験に落ちてしまったのは残念だ。
examples.english: He surely studied very hard, but it's a shame he failed the exam.
examples.breakdown: Used to express regret or disappointment about a situation that didn't turn out as expected, despite a strong effort.

examples.japanese: こんなに美味しいケーキなのに、誰も手をつけようとしないなんて、不思議だろうに。
examples.english: Even though this cake is so delicious, it's strange that no one is trying to eat it.
examples.breakdown: Expresses bewilderment or surprise that something that should be desirable is not being taken advantage of.

examples.japanese: あの時、もっと早く連絡してあげればよかったのに。
examples.english: I should have contacted him sooner at that time.
examples.breakdown: Expresses regret about a past action or inaction, implying a missed opportunity or a better outcome if a different choice had been made.

examples.japanese: 彼女は忙しいだろうに、わざわざ私のために時間を作ってくれた。
examples.english: She must be busy, but she went out of her way to make time for me.
examples.breakdown: Used to express appreciation or surprise at someone's effort, acknowledging their potential difficulties or inconveniences.

examples.japanese: もっと練習すれば、優勝できたはずなのに、油断してしまったのが敗因だ。
examples.english: If I had practiced more, I should have been able to win, but my carelessness was the cause of my defeat.
examples.breakdown: Expresses a strong belief that a better outcome was possible if a different approach had been taken, highlighting a missed opportunity due to a mistake.

N1.pattern: であれ / であろうと

examples.japanese: どんな困難であれ、彼は決して諦めないだろう。
examples.english: Whatever difficulties there may be, he will never give up.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses 「であれ」 after a noun phrase 「どんな困難」 to mean 'whatever difficulties'.

examples.japanese: 誰であれ、この規則を破ることは許されない。
examples.english: Whoever it may be, breaking this rule is not allowed.
examples.breakdown: 「誰であれ」 means 'whoever it may be', emphasizing that the rule applies to everyone without exception.

examples.japanese: 結果がどうであろうと、私たちは全力を尽くした。
examples.english: However the results may turn out, we did our best.
examples.breakdown: 「どうであろうと」 is used to express indifference to the outcome, meaning 'however it may be'.

examples.japanese: たとえそれがどんなに小さなことగానే思われようと、無視してはならない。
examples.english: Even if it may seem like a small thing, it must not be ignored.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses 「ようと」 (a contraction of 「であろうと」) to mean 'even if it may seem'.

examples.japanese: どんな理由であれ、遅刻は認められません。
examples.english: For whatever reason, lateness will not be permitted.
examples.breakdown: 「どんな理由であれ」 means 'for whatever reason', indicating that no excuse will be accepted.

examples.japanese: 成功であれ失敗であれ、この経験から多くを学ぶことができるだろう。
examples.english: Whether it's success or failure, we will likely be able to learn a lot from this experience.
examples.breakdown: The pattern 'であれ〜であれ' is used to connect two contrasting or alternative possibilities, indicating that something applies regardless of which option is true.

examples.japanese: どんな理由であれ、約束を破るのは許されないことだ。
examples.english: No matter the reason, breaking a promise is unforgivable.
examples.breakdown: Here, 'どんな理由であれ' emphasizes that the reason is irrelevant; the action of breaking a promise is unacceptable in any case.

examples.japanese: 子供であれ大人であれ、誰もが尊重されるべき権利を持っている。
examples.english: Whether a child or an adult, everyone has the right to be respected.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses the pattern to state a universal truth that applies to all individuals, regardless of their age.

examples.japanese: 賛成であれ反対であれ、まずは自分の意見をしっかり表明することが大切だ。
examples.english: Whether you agree or disagree, it's important to clearly express your own opinion first.
examples.breakdown: The pattern highlights that the act of expressing one's opinion is crucial, irrespective of whether that opinion is supportive or critical.

examples.japanese: 雨であれ晴れであれ、明日のピクニックは予定通り実施します。
examples.english: Whether it rains or shines, tomorrow's picnic will proceed as planned.
examples.breakdown: This sentence shows that the plan remains unchanged regardless of the weather conditions.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトは、新たな挑戦でもあり、これまでの経験を活かす機会でもあります。
examples.english: This project is both a new challenge and an opportunity to leverage our past experience.
examples.breakdown: The pattern 'でもあり〜でもある' is used to connect two nouns or noun phrases, indicating that something possesses both qualities or characteristics.

examples.japanese: 彼は長年研究者として活躍する傍ら、作家としても多くの読者を魅了してきました。
examples.english: While active as a researcher for many years, he has also captivated many readers as an author.
examples.breakdown: Here, '〜傍ら' and '〜でもあり〜でもある' are used to show that someone has two roles or activities simultaneously.

examples.japanese: その都市は、歴史的な建造物でもあり、最先端のテクノロジーが集まる場所でもあります。
examples.english: That city is both a place with historical buildings and a hub for cutting-edge technology.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses the pattern to describe a place that has two contrasting or complementary features.

examples.japanese: 彼女の態度は、親切でもあり、同時に少し突き放したようでもありました。
examples.english: Her attitude was both kind and, at the same time, seemed a little distant.
examples.breakdown: The pattern is used to express that someone's behavior or demeanor has two different aspects.

examples.japanese: この仕事は、やりがいのあるものでもあり、精神的に疲れるものでもあります。
examples.english: This job is both rewarding and mentally exhausting.
examples.breakdown: This sentence illustrates the pattern being used to describe a situation or job that has both positive and negative aspects.

N1.pattern: でも何でもない /くも何ともない
N1.romanization: demo nan demo nai / kumo nan tomo nai
N1.meaning: not in the least; nothing like that

examples.japanese: 彼は忙しいと言っていたが、実際にはたいした仕事でも何でもなかった。
examples.english: He said he was busy, but in reality, it wasn't even that much work.
examples.breakdown: Used after a noun (仕事) to deny it being significant or important.

examples.japanese: その話は冗談でも何でもなく、彼は真剣にそう思っているようだ。
examples.english: That story wasn't a joke or anything like that; he seems to genuinely think so.
examples.breakdown: Used after a noun (冗談) to negate it being that thing, emphasizing seriousness.

examples.japanese: 彼女の態度は冷たいように見えたが、話してみると親切で、心配するようなことでも何でもなかった。
examples.english: Her attitude seemed cold, but when I talked to her, she was kind, and there was nothing to worry about.
examples.breakdown: Used after a noun phrase (心配するようなこと) to dismiss it as not being a cause for concern.

examples.japanese: この問題は複雑に見えるかもしれないが、よく考えれば難しいことでも何でもない。
examples.english: This problem might look complicated, but if you think about it carefully, it's not difficult at all.
examples.breakdown: Used after a noun phrase (難しいこと) to indicate it's not as difficult as it appears.

examples.japanese: 彼は自分の失敗を恥ずかしいことでも何でもないかのように振る舞っていた。
examples.english: He acted as if his failure was nothing to be ashamed of.
examples.breakdown: Used after a noun phrase (恥ずかしいこと) to show someone is pretending something isn't a big deal.

examples.japanese: この感動的なパフォーマンスを見て、涙が出ない人がいるだろうか。まさに芸術でなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: Is there anyone who wouldn't shed tears watching this moving performance? It is truly art, and nothing else.
examples.breakdown: The pattern emphasizes that the performance is undeniably art, using a rhetorical question to reinforce the point.

examples.japanese: 長年培ってきた経験と知識を活かさずに、どうして成果が出せるというのか。それは怠慢でなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: How can one achieve results without utilizing the experience and knowledge cultivated over many years? That is nothing but laziness.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses the pattern to strongly assert that not using one's accumulated experience is a form of laziness.

examples.japanese: これほどまでに人の心を掴む物語は、そうそうない。奇跡でなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: A story that captures people's hearts to this extent is rare. It is nothing short of a miracle.
examples.breakdown: The pattern is used here to express awe and wonder, concluding that the story's impact is miraculous.

examples.japanese: 毎日のように不平不満ばかり言っている彼に、仕事のやりがいを感じていると言われても信じられない。それは単なる強がりでなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: Even if he says he finds his job rewarding, I can't believe him when he complains every day. That is nothing but bravado.
examples.breakdown: The speaker uses the pattern to dismiss the person's claim as mere pretense, given their constant complaining.

examples.japanese: あれだけ努力を重ねた結果、この成功を収めたのだ。運が良かっただけでなくてなんだろう。
examples.english: After all the effort put in, this success was achieved. It is more than just luck.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses the pattern to highlight that the success is due to more than just luck, implying significant effort.

N1.meaning: isn't it; I wonder if it’s not ~

examples.japanese: この状況は、我々の努力が足りなかったことの表れではあるまいか。
examples.english: Isn't this situation a reflection of our insufficient efforts?
examples.breakdown: Used to express a thought or suspicion that something might be the case, often with a hint of doubt or self-reflection.

examples.japanese: 彼が急に会社を辞めたのは、何か大きな計画があるからではあるまいか。
examples.english: Isn't it that he suddenly quit the company because he has some big plan?
examples.breakdown: Expresses a conjecture or speculation about someone's actions or motivations.

examples.japanese: こんなに美しい夕焼けは、まるで絵画のようではないか。
examples.english: Isn't such a beautiful sunset like a painting?
examples.breakdown: This sentence is not using the pattern 'ではあるまいか'. It uses the pattern '～ではないか' which has a similar nuance of rhetorical question but is less formal and expresses admiration.

examples.japanese: 長年の夢だった世界一周旅行、本当に実現するのだろうか。いや、きっと実現するのではあるまいか。
examples.english: My lifelong dream of traveling around the world, will it really come true? No, I wonder if it won't truly come true.
examples.breakdown: Used to express a strong hope or conviction that something will happen, framed as a rhetorical question to emphasize the belief.

examples.japanese: 最近の若者の間で流行しているこの音楽、将来的に古典と呼ばれるようになるのではあるまいか。
examples.english: This music that's popular among young people these days, won't it become considered classic in the future?
examples.breakdown: Used to speculate about future trends or developments, suggesting a possibility that might seem unlikely but is worth considering.

N1.meaning: it’s not like; it isn’t as if ~

examples.japanese: 彼は新米社員ではあるまいし、基本的なビジネスマナーくらいは心得ているはずだ。
examples.english: He's not a new employee, so he should know basic business etiquette.
examples.breakdown: Connects a noun/na-adjective to the pattern to negate the assumption that the person is inexperienced.

examples.japanese: この程度の遅刻で大騒ぎするなんて、子供ではあるまいし、もう少し落ち着いてほしい。
examples.english: To make such a fuss over this level of lateness, it's not like you're a child; I want you to calm down a bit.
examples.breakdown: Used with a noun to express that the person's behavior is inappropriate for their age or maturity level.

examples.japanese: プロの料理人ではあるまいし、家庭でそこまで完璧な味を再現するのは難しいだろう。
examples.english: It's not like you're a professional chef, so it's probably difficult to perfectly recreate that taste at home.
examples.breakdown: Used with a noun to state that the current situation or skill level is not that of a professional.

examples.japanese: 彼女はただの友人ではあるまいし、なぜあんなに嫉妬するのか理解できない。
examples.english: It's not like she's just a friend, so I can't understand why she's so jealous.
examples.breakdown: Used with a noun to imply a deeper relationship than what is being presented or assumed.

examples.japanese: 経験者ではあるまいし、最初から全てを理解しろというのは無理な話だ。
examples.english: It's not like you're an experienced person, so it's unreasonable to expect you to understand everything from the start.
examples.breakdown: Used with a noun to reject the expectation of expertise or prior knowledge.

examples.japanese: 今回の無責任な行動は、ただ謝って済むようなことではない。重大な結果を招くだろう。
examples.english: This irresponsible behavior won't be settled with just an apology; it will lead to serious consequences.
examples.breakdown: The pattern '〜て済まない' is used here with the verb '謝る' (to apologize) to indicate that a simple apology is insufficient to resolve the situation.

examples.japanese: 彼の度重なる遅刻は、もはや軽い注意で済むレベルを超えている。
examples.english: His repeated lateness has gone beyond the level where a light warning would suffice.
examples.breakdown: The pattern '〜で済む' is used with '注意' (warning) to express that a mere warning is no longer enough to address the problem.

examples.japanese: 約束を破ったことに対して、彼がどんなに謝罪しても、それでは済まないだろう。信頼関係は失われたのだから。
examples.english: No matter how much he apologizes for breaking his promise, it probably won't be enough; the trust has been lost.
examples.breakdown: Here, '〜では済まない' is used to emphasize that an apology alone cannot mend the broken trust.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトの失敗は、個人のミスとして片付けられるものではなく、組織全体の責任問題として議論されるべきだ。それで済まない。
examples.english: The failure of this project is not something that can be dismissed as an individual's mistake; it should be discussed as an issue of the entire organization's responsibility. It won't end there.
examples.breakdown: The phrase '〜では済まない' is used to convey that the issue is more complex and won't be resolved by simply attributing it to a single person's error.

examples.japanese: 長年積み上げてきた努力が、たった一度のミスで水の泡となるような状況では、努力した意味がなくなってしまう。それでは済まない。
examples.english: In a situation where years of accumulated effort are ruined by a single mistake, the effort would lose its meaning. It won't end with just that.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses '〜では済まない' to express that the outcome is unacceptable and that the effort invested should not be rendered meaningless by a single failure.

examples.japanese: どんなに努力しても、この難問はどうにも解けなかった。
examples.english: No matter how hard I tried, I couldn't solve this difficult problem by any means.
examples.breakdown: どうにも～ない is used to emphasize that something cannot be done, no matter what efforts are made.

examples.japanese: 彼はあまりにも頑固なので、どうにも説得することができない。
examples.english: He is so stubborn that I cannot persuade him by any means.
examples.breakdown: This sentence uses どうにも～ない to express the inability to persuade someone due to their stubbornness.

examples.japanese: いくら調べても、その事件の真相はどうにも掴めなかった。
examples.english: No matter how much I investigated, I couldn't grasp the truth of that incident by any means.
examples.breakdown: The pattern highlights the persistent failure to understand or uncover the truth, despite thorough investigation.

examples.japanese: この古いパソコンは、どうにも起動しなくなってしまった。
examples.english: This old computer has stopped working by any means.
examples.breakdown: Used here to describe a complete and unresolvable failure of the computer to start up.

examples.japanese: 彼女の態度はあまりにも無責任で、どうにも許せなかった。
examples.english: Her attitude was so irresponsible that I couldn't forgive her by any means.
examples.breakdown: This sentence expresses a strong inability to forgive someone's behavior due to its extreme irresponsibility.

N1.meaning: no sooner than; as soon as ~

examples.japanese: 終業のベルが鳴るが早いか、彼はオフィスを飛び出した。
examples.english: No sooner had the closing bell rung than he dashed out of the office.
examples.breakdown: Verb (past tense) + が早いか: Used to express that one action happened immediately after another.

examples.japanese: 彼女は新しいプロジェクトのアイデアが浮かぶが早いか、すぐにチームに共有した。
examples.english: As soon as she came up with an idea for the new project, she immediately shared it with the team.
examples.breakdown: Verb (past tense) + が早いか: Indicates that the second action followed the first without any delay.

examples.japanese: 試験が終わるが早いか、学生たちは一斉に教室から出て行った。
examples.english: No sooner had the exam finished than the students poured out of the classroom all at once.
examples.breakdown: Verb (past tense) + が早いか: Emphasizes the immediacy of the students' exit after the exam concluded.

examples.japanese: 週末の予定が決まるが早いか、彼は友人に連絡を取り始めた。
examples.english: As soon as the weekend plans were decided, he started contacting his friends.
examples.breakdown: Verb (past tense) + が早いか: Shows that the action of contacting friends happened right after the plans were finalized.

examples.japanese: 飛行機が着陸するが早いか、乗客たちは手荷物を受け取るために列を作った。
examples.english: No sooner had the plane landed than the passengers formed a line to collect their luggage.
examples.breakdown: Verb (past tense) + が早いか: Describes the immediate action of the passengers after the plane's landing.

examples.japanese: この仕事は楽なら楽でいいが、給料が安いなら、生活していくのが難しいだろう。
examples.english: If this job were easy, that would be good, but if the salary is low, it will be difficult to make a living.
examples.breakdown: The pattern connects two negative conditions: the job being easy, but the salary being low, implying a difficult situation.

examples.japanese: 彼が親切なら親切で助かるが、その親切が裏目に出るなら、むしろ迷惑だ。
examples.english: If he were kind, that would be helpful, but if that kindness backfires, it's rather a nuisance.
examples.breakdown: This sentence contrasts the positive aspect of kindness with the negative outcome if it backfires, using the pattern to express this conditional negativity.

examples.japanese: 時間が自由なら自由でいいが、お金がなければ、どこにも行けないだろう。
